brief: Breadth is deteriorating even as the AI trade dominates: 400 S&P stocks sit below their 50-day average and the market trades 'long AI, short AI irrelevance.' BofA's Bull & Bear Indicator fell to 8.8 from 9.3 (Sell), driven by wider high-yield spreads, HY outflows, and global breadth at its worst since March. The desk calls this risk-off until the dollar peaks: the dollar is spiking on credit-event risk, flagged via AUD/JPY, French bonds, risk parity and tech CDS, but open-ended Treasury buyback/yield-curve-control policy panic limits the downside because policymakers cannot let yields threaten the AI capex boom before the midterms, unless small and mid-caps break down with banks. On the AI-bubble question, the bull case ('it's the railroads this time') notes AI's market concentration is still below railroads' 1881 peak and capex is a smaller share of GDP, with chip prices rising rather than deflating like freight rates did; the bear case notes railroad booms were backstopped by falling yields, which is not the case today. Separately, BofA turns contrarian-bullish on bonds ('buy humiliation'), citing historically negative long-run Treasury returns as an entry signal and flagging hyperscaler bond yields (Oracle 8.4%, Meta 7.5%) as eventually tempting given AI's implicit government backstop.
